title: Shinsekai Yori: The Impure Cat
alt: Dusk in a village of wooden houses by a canal. The sky is gold at the horizon, then rose, then violet, with the first stars. At the right is a long school hall with lit paper screens under a great tiled roof. On the ridge of the roof stands a huge thin black cat with very long legs, a long neck and a long hooked tail. Its eye shines red, and it looks down. Below at the left a small child runs along the canal path with a paper lantern. Over the child a thick straw rope with white folded papers hangs between two poles, and one pole has two horn loudspeakers. At the far left are a thatched farmhouse and a water wheel. Rice fields full of water lie behind. A boat is tied up in the canal, and fireflies are out near the reeds.
summary: A painting of the impure cat from Shinsekai Yori in {strokes} brush strokes, with a playback of each stroke.
text: This is the impure cat, from Shinsekai Yori (From the New World), the novel by Yusuke Kishi. A thousand years from now, the village of Kamisu 66 is quiet and kind. Every person in it has a power that can kill. So the village watches its children, and a child who may go wrong does not grow up.

The cat is the thing that comes for such a child. The village made it from house cats: it is three meters long, with legs and a neck that are much too long. The children think that it is only a story to make them go home before dark. Here the going-home song plays from the horns at dusk, and one child is late. The painting has {strokes} brush strokes.
